evidence.claim: The November 24, 2026 date for Steve Lacy's Oh yeah? Tour at Bill Graham Civic Auditorium is officially sold out.
A second Steve Lacy concert was added on November 25 at Bill Graham Civic Auditorium due to overwhelming popular demand.
Primary inventory for Steve Lacy at Bill Graham Civic Auditorium sold out completely, shifting ticketing entirely to secondary resale.

demand.compared_with_the_others: This event will draw more people than Song Dongye's performance but fewer than the Warriors game, filling Bill Graham Civic Auditorium to its 8,500 capacity.

plan.audience: Mostly 18-30 fans of Steve Lacy's alt-R&B/indie sound. Most are San Francisco locals, with a sizeable share coming from the East Bay and Peninsula/South Bay. SF residents tend to walk, take Muni or use ride-hail; regional fans lean on BART.
plan.attendance_reason: Three sourced claims say the show is officially sold out at the 8,500 capacity, primary inventory is gone and a second night (Nov 25) was added for demand. The venue is indoor, so a full house is expected; resale no-shows are small and within noise.
plan.reference_reason: Coliseum is the only measured venue where the BART station is effectively at the door, which matches Civic Center station sitting across the plaza from the auditorium. EMBR (15-minute walk) and DBRK (20-25-minute uphill walk) have much weaker station access. The COLS night profile also matches a weeknight evening event.
multiplier_reasons: Parking: only some garages downtown, far less than the Coliseum's huge lot, which pushes share up.
Walk: across the plaza from CIVC, as close as or closer than the Coliseum footbridge, which pushes share up.
Crowd type: a young concert crowd is more transit-inclined than a baseball crowd, which pushes share up.

Competing transit: Muni Metro and buses on Market, walkable SF neighborhoods and heavy ride-hail all compete for the many SF-resident attendees. The Coliseum has almost no non-car alternative to BART, so this pulls share down strongly.

Time of day: a Tuesday show ending near 23:00 close to BART's last trains pushes some return trips to ride-hail, which pulls share down. These factors roughly cancel against COLS, so the multiplier stays at 1.0.
plan.arrival_reason: Doors are likely around 19:00, so the peak is the 19:00 hour. There is no tailgating, so early arrivals are small. Support acts play from 20:00 and the headliner likely starts after 21:00, so many fans arrive during the opener and some after 21:00. A large weekday commute background sits in the -3/-2 hours, but few concertgoers travel then.
plan.end_reason: An 8pm start with support acts and a headliner set typically wraps around 22:45-23:00 at this venue.
plan.departure_reason: Most of the crowd exits as the show ends and crosses the plaza to CIVC in the 23:00 hour to catch the last trains. Some leave during the encore or late set to make suburban connections. Almost nothing falls after midnight because BART service ends.
plan.weather_reason: Only 0.3 mm of rain, about 16 C, indoor venue, sold out. The weather has no meaningful effect on turnout.

other_stations.why: One stop away near Union Square; some fans eat or drink there before the show and board or exit there.
Transbay trains after 23:00 will carry a noticeable concert load through West Oakland toward the East Bay.
Mission-district fans may come in from nearby Mission stations instead of walking.

risks: No concert reference exists; the COLS-based share could be off substantially in either direction.
Heavy ride-hail use late at night may lower departure share below arrival share.
If the headliner runs past 23:15, departures crowd against last trains, and some riders shift to ride-hail or are clipped at midnight.
Thanksgiving week (Tuesday before) may change commute background and travel patterns.
Platform crowding at CIVC after the show could delay exits into later in the hour.

overrides.why: Coliseum riders have no real alternative to BART besides driving. Civic Center faces strong Muni, walking and ride-hail competition from a largely SF-resident crowd, plus late-night return leakage. The specialist counted the pluses but understated this competition.
At concerts with openers, many fans skip early sets and arrive for the headliner after 21:00. The specialist's late tail was too thin.
With a 23:00 end, the +1 hour is after midnight, when BART is closed, so 17% there would be lost. Early leavers racing last trains belong in the 22:00 hour.

plan._reasoning:
I'm weighing which station to use as the reference point. Coliseum station is the closest access, but its share is only 14.3%, since that area is mostly East Bay suburban riders who lean on BART. Civic Center has plenty of alternatives right across the plaza in downtown SF, and the concert crowd is young and drawn from all over the Bay Area, so I'm adjusting the Coliseum figure by about 1.3 times.

I'm settling on a multiplier of about 1.0 for the Coliseum figure, since the Civic Center crowd has Muni and walking as strong alternatives, which offsets the parking and young-crowd advantages. That gives roughly 14.3% of arrivals, around 1,215 people. I'm also working out the timing profile, with most arrivals clustered in the hour or so before the headliner.

I'm checking the end time next: 23:00 looks right, and most people leave in that hour, with a smaller share around 22:00 and some trailing past midnight. The departure split comes out to roughly 12% in the hour before, 85% in the hour of 23:00, and the rest just after, since last BART trains from Civic Center leave around midnight.

I'm checking the departure split against the arrival share, since late-night ride-hail could push it a bit, though I'm keeping a single multiplier. Attendance stays at 8,500, and I'm looking at whether the transbay trains toward Oakland are the other stations worth mentioning.

I'm checking the remaining station options and the Thanksgiving date, which falls on the Tuesday before. I'm leaning toward a "low" confidence label for the overrides, since the multiplier rests on reasoning with no concert reference behind it.
